Go with this pump. OEM pumps have more laminations in the motor stator which apparentlly makes them run cooler and longer. We have a washer/ dryer combo unit. 10 yrs old and still works well. So far, only part that has gone bad is this dump pump. Usually every 6-8 months. We use the heck out of the machine, tho. Do yourself a favor and clean out the condenser and blower wheel when you change the pump. Lots of lint accumulates on these two parts over a years time and since the machine is apart and on its side, might as well. Makes a significant difference in the drying times. Just be patient and keep track of what screws came out of what holes. :)

There are so many of these pumps on Amazon that it is difficult to know which is OEM, authentic, or otherwise. I paid $29 for a pump from A+ Supply, and the description explicitly says that it is an authentic LG part. I can confirm that it is. My pump came in a brown package with a label and bar code for an "LG #XXXXXXX". Don't be put off by the box--it is a "track pack" intended for service professionals rather than consumers. (Consumer packs would have pictures, descriptions, and instructions.) Moreover, the part itself has "PLASET" molded in--that is the Italian manufacturer, and it matches the mold marks on the the old pump and the recirculation pump. It slid in perfectly, and everything lined up with no hitches. Once I got it back together, the washer is as good as new.

If your LG washer displays the OE error, that indicates a pump failure; my original pump failed when the impeller cracked and was rattling around inside the bell housing. If you get that error and it has a loud sound, it is probably a similar issue. Rather than taking the entire machine apart, tip it up and back. I was able to replace the pump by coming up through the open bottom of the machine. It was a bit tight, but very doable.

I'm giving it two-stars because it fit and I hope it works for longer than some of the failed reviews here. Having said that. My LG is working again and all it cost me was $26 and an hour of my time.
For those about to attempt to replace your pump, there are two ways. Through the bottom or remove the front panel. I removed the front panel only because there was no room to tip the machine on its side. There are half a dozen YouTube videos showing how. BUT what they don't show you is how difficult it is to put the door boot gasket back on. There's a steel wire that's spring loaded to hold the boot in place. It requires a special spreader tool to expand it far enough to slip on. Since I didn't have one I improvised and asked for help. It took three hands and three flat head screwdrivers to pry it back on. Just put the ring on as far as you can by hand and then slowly wedge the ring down. Easy peasy. In all it's less than an hours work.
